summary: E72 predicted .le-st.ok (L92) as next --wh candidate (hash-valid entry ≈ verification outcome → ⚪ REPLAYABLE). Audit finds this is INCORRECT: the .le-st state machine models ADMISSION STATES not hash-validity. Two states only: .le-st.ok (admitted, L92 → --grn) and .le-st.pending (not yet admitted, L93 → --amb). No .le-st.fail or .le-st.invalid class exists. Absence of a failure class confirms 'OK' means 'admission succeeded' not 'hash-chain checked'. Entries displayed (surface_commit, E05_geo_claim, helen2027_v1, HOME_9.2_ship, starship_v3) are actual operator-admitted ledger writes via helen_say.py. Conclusion: .le-st.ok → --grn (🟢 ADMITTED) is semantically CORRECT. Contrast with E71 (.vr-v.pass = gate verification, no admission event → --wh) and E72 (CLEAN = tree clearance, no admission event → --wh). Boundary established: --grn is correct where an admission event occurred; --wh is correct where only a verification/clearance outcome occurred without an admission event.
